claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Thank you for reaching out! I'll guide you through the Child Benefit eligibility assessment.

To start, I need to know about the child or children you're asking about:

**How old is your child?** This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply:
- Under 16 years old
- Between 16 and 19 years old
- 20 years or older

Please let me know the age of the child you're inquiring about.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll continue with the assessment based on your situation profile. You're asking about Alex, who is 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Since Alex is 17 years old, they fall in the 16-19 age bracket. For children this age, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether they're in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In approved education or training** (such as full-time non-advanced education at school or college)?
2. **Has recently left education** (within the last 20 weeks)?
3. **Neither** - not in education/training and didn't recently leave?

Could you let me know which applies to Alex?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Based on your situation profile, Alex is 17 years old and is **not in approved education or in an extension period**. Let me continue the assessment with this information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the assessment, I need to provide you with the eligibility determination:

**Eligibility Result: NOT ELIGIBLE**

**Why this decision was reached:**

For Alex (age 17), Child Benefit eligibility requires that children aged 16-19 must be in **approved education or training**. Since Alex is:
- 17 years old (in the 16-19 age bracket)
- NOT currently in approved education or training
- NOT in an extension period (which applies to young people who recently left education)

Alex does not meet the qualifying child criteria for Child Benefit.

**Important Information:**

- Children under 16 automatically qualify (Alex is over 16)
- Children aged 16-19 must be in approved full-time non-advanced education or training
- If a 16-17 year old has recently left education, benefit can continue for up to 20 weeks if they register with careers services or the armed services

**What you could consider:**

- If Alex enrolls in approved education or training in the future, you may become eligible at that point
- If Alex has recently left education (within the last 20 weeks) and has registered with careers services, there may be an extension period available
